I will start from what worked for me last year and only adjust a little. On 66 mu, I cannot afford to gamble. Wheat and maize are still my backbone, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and use the rest for stevia and sweet potato to spread income. I have well irrigation, so I will push yield a bit on wheat and maize with enough fertilizer and timely watering. I did middle school, so I do look at balance, not only habit: wheat needs a steady base and topdressing, maize needs strong nitrogen but I will not leave out phosphorus and potassium, and the cash crops need cleaner fields and more careful pesticide timing. Around here, if fertilizer looks a little heavy, I can still accept that cost; if yield falls, that hurts much more. So this year I will put 50 mu into wheat-maize rotation, 8 mu into stevia, and 8 mu into sweet potato, using improved or hybrid seed where I have seen good field performance nearby.
